steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (a field name in an interface others call), so I'm flagging before editing rather than making the change.

The change itself is one line: `routes/users.js:6`, `userId:` → `user_id:`.

The consequence: this is a breaking change to the `GET /users` response contract. `README.md` names three consumers — the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export — and states that field names are part of the contract and that changes go through a versioned endpoint. Any consumer reading `userId` gets `undefined` after this; the shipped iOS clients can't be updated in lockstep, and the partner export would break on its next nightly run.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
